notes.title: Train World: Two Years On
notes.content:
🚂 Train World – Celebrating 2 Years + Ongoing Updates Recap 🚂
Hello Engineers,

On June 20, Train World officially marked its 2-year anniversary! 🥳🥳🥳

Since launch, we've released dozens of updates improving visuals, stability, mechanics, and overall gameplay. With your feedback and support, the game has grown into a robust simulation experience for train fans around the world.

Below is a full recap of all updates released since the last announcement.
🔧 Tunnels, Camera & Terrain Improvements
Added fully-modeled tunnel interiors with electrification wires.

Improved camera behavior in drive mode – no more sudden jumps when entering tunnels.

Fixed gaps in tunnel interiors on long curves.

Fixed tunnel entrance model and added proper collision checking to prevent overlapping tunnels.

Added error messages for invalid construction involving tunnels.

Fixed wall clipping and camera movement issues inside tunnels.

Fixed rare rail snapping and overlapping track placement bugs.
🚆 Coupling & Train Layouts
Added the "Pre-place wagons" option – wagons are placed instantly at uncoupling points when launching the train.

Trains now revert to default layouts (as set in the train editor) when sent to the depot.

Updated coupling/uncoupling tutorial to reflect new features.

Added error message when wagon pre-placement fails due to blocked rails.
🛤️ Rail Building & Logic Updates
Added "Straight Rail" modifier (default: Ctrl) – works for single and double rails.

Updated rail overlay to be color-coded during upgrades.

Removed unnecessary path recalculations when editing trains – eliminates jumpy behavior.

Reduced snapping to lines and improved waypoint editing validation.

Fixed various UI and construction tool quirks on all maps.
🎨 Model Upgrades – Locomotives & Wagons
Nearly every train model in the game has received a visual upgrade over the past months:

Updated bogie geometry.

Closed gaps visible from underneath.

Fixed minor model issues across dozens of steam, diesel, and electric locomotives.

All passenger and freight wagons have been revised.
📘 Research & Tutorial Fixes
Fixed Portola locomotive research cost.

Fixed rare errors during \era transitions\ or first-time loads.

Improved research tree scroll behavior – now focuses on newly unlocked items even across gaps.

Fixed research tutorial flow and starting conditions in certain regions.
🛠️ General Fixes & Optimizations
Fixed disappearing trees, water circle artifacts, and tooltip inconsistencies.

Fixed train edit filter panel reset and waypoint placement issues.

Fixed cargo type loading options not appearing properly.

Optimized performance when managing hundreds of trains on large maps.

Fixed bugs when editing or launching trains with "Poor" power-to-weight ratios.

Resolved issues with production chains not serviced by existing trains.

Tutorial text corrections and improved clarity.

Updated session-based achievements
🗺️ New Content
Added new map: Ironpeak Pass.
🧭 Looking Ahead
As the sole developer behind Train World, it’s been a deeply rewarding experience growing this game with you over the past two years. While I won’t have time for major new content development in the near future, I remain committed to: active bug fixing, performance improvements, and timely support for all players.



Thank you again for your continued enthusiasm and support! Here's to many more miles of track ahead! 🚂

notes.title: Train World Update — Coupling & Uncoupling Arrives!
notes.content:
A major new gameplay feature is here: manual wagon coupling and uncoupling! This update brings deeper control, new waypoint tools, new locomotives, and dozens of improvements and fixes.
🔩 New Features & Mechanics

 Coupling and Uncoupling of Wagons - trains can now uncouple and re-couple wagons at designated waypoints. Coupling is only possible with wagons that were previously uncoupled. Includes new sounds, a tutorial, and error handling for uncoupled locomotives.
 Trains Without Wagons or Locomotives Remain on Tracks - wagons without locomotives stay on the  rails, and locomotive-only trains can move independently
 Movement in Reverse - available at waypoints where a train changes direction (signals and passenger stations). Enables more advanced route setups.
 Coupling & Uncoupling Tutorial - a step-by-step guide that walks players through how to manage this new mechanic.

🚦 Waypoint System Updates

 Priority Load - when enabled, a train will prioritize loading cargo/passengers specifically for the selected connection.
 Wait for Full Train - train waits until fully loaded (based on selected percentage or amount) with any available cargo/passengers.
 Waypoint UI - updated Waypoint Settings Interface and new icons for active options like “Full train”. Now waypoint settings can be edited without entering route edit mode

🚆 New Locomotives

 0-8-0 USRA (2nd Era Steam)
 SDP40F (3rd Era Diesel)

⚙️ Gameplay Improvements

 Updated steam engine stats (power, speed, and price now reflect historical data)
 Adjusted one-time contract cargo amounts and rewards
 Population growth tuning (affects production)
 Adjusted production rates for Aluminum and Machines industries
 Optimized CPU and memory usage in train simulation
 Large train list display performance significantly improved
 Added UI scaling setting

🎨 Visual & UI Updates

 Updated loading screen backgrounds
 Updated brick tunnel entrance model
 Fixed missing shadows in cities
 Adjusted shadow distance parameters
 Updated general UI style
 Time labels added to “Full Load” and “Wait for Connection”
 Labels added to the age graph in "Replace" and "Inventory" panels

🧰 Fixes

 Resolved issue with trains getting stuck at stations with specific waypoint configurations
 Fixed “Mastering the Research Tree” tutorial
 Resolved game hang on failed save file load
 Fixed train stopping abruptly at signals
 Train jumping when editing active routes
 Trains no longer stop on signal waypoints when load conditions are already met
 Incorrect cargo/passenger display after removing trains
 Fixed long locomotives hanging off rails
 Fixed display issues with stations, depots, signals, and contract connections
 Corrected one-time contract cargo amount display
 Resolved incorrect wait time calculations for full train/connection options
 Max wait time for auto-wait and full load set to 90 minutes
 Resolved flipped values in the “Targets and Statistics” panel
 Fixed game freezing on save files with corrupted rails
 Train display and payments are now correctly handled
 Fixed UI waypoint button error
 Fixed freight priority logic
 Fixed rail placement for locomotives
 Trains now properly resume movement after signal wait with fulfilled load condition
 Various language fixes

🛤️ This first implementation of wagon coupling/uncoupling lays the foundation for more interesting features. Stay tuned for future updates!

💬 Let me know how you’re using coupling in your networks!
Your feedback drives development — join the conversation and share your creations.

notes.title: New Features & Steam Locomotives!
notes.content:
Hello, Railway Managers!
The past few weeks have been packed with updates, and I am excited to bring you a massive list of improvements, optimizations, and new features for Train World! From quality-of-life upgrades to brand-new locomotives, there's a lot to cover—so let's dive in.
🚂 New Steam Locomotives

 0-6-0 Portola (Era 1)
 2-10-4 Texas (Era 2)
 2-8-4 Berkshire (Era 2)
 4-6-2 Pacific (Era 1)
📊 Industries & Production Panel

 New UI to track all available industries across your unlocked regions
 View available production chains and plan your industry expansions with ease
🛠 Major Optimizations & Fixes

 New "Sell excess wagons" toggle in the Replace panel—excess wagons are automatically sold if the new train setup doesn't match length requirements
 Updated train panels with larger Replace and Inventory sections
 "Remove all" button added to quickly clear train layouts
 Improved route visualization—now you can track the current train's route in Follow Camera mode
 Pathfinding Optimizations—significantly reduced memory usage and improved performance, especially with large train networks (50+ trains)
 Fixed multiple issues, including saved game loading errors, passenger display issues, and waypoint auto-wait errors
🎛 Enhanced User Controls & Customization

 New train pause mechanic—trains can now be stopped at waypoints without requiring a route edit
 Updated train panels—Replace and Waypoint panels are now more user-friendly, plus you can now select multiple save files for deletion
 New "Auto-renew on low lifespan" toggle—when enabled, trains with low lifespan will auto-renew if possible
🌍 Enhanced Visuals & Immersion

 Updated terrain modifications for bridges, tunnels, and tracks, fixing grass patches and terrain edges
 Stylized background images added to the loading screen for a fresh new look
 Updated biomes & improved animal placement for better visual realism
 Updated rail color coding in Map View & Minimap for better clarity
 Inside train sound effects! Experience the rush of being onboard with realistic train horns (H key) and new follow-camera wind sounds
🔧 QoL Upgrades & Bug Fixes

 New graphics settings: Toggle sun movement and cloud shadows
 New alphabetical sorting for the Connections list
 Waypoint UI improvements—Updated Remove button position to reduce misclicks
 Fixed missing passengers—Passengers now appear correctly on stations even after reloading a save
 Fixed various errors with routes, train lists, waypoints, localization, and UI interactions
 These updates are all designed to improve your gameplay experience, whether it's optimizing train performance, enhancing visuals, or making management easier. We’re continuing to refine Train World based on your feedback, so keep those suggestions coming!
🚆 What’s next?
I am already working on new gameplay mechanics, locomotives, and optimizations that will further enhance your railway empire. Stay tuned for more updates, and don’t forget to share your thoughts!

See you on the rail tracks! 🚆🔥

notes.title: 🚂 Silverstream Update & More! 🌟
notes.content:
Hello, Train World community!
I’m thrilled to share some exciting updates and improvements we’ve made recently. These changes are designed to enhance your gameplay experience and add new depth to the world of Train World. Let’s dive into what’s new!
🌍New Content:

 Silverstream Bay Map: Explore this charming new map featuring a central shipping lane, picturesque mountain ranges, and a flowing river.
🛠️Gameplay Enhancements:

 Wagons Panel: Easily view available cargo types and compatible wagons with the new Wagons panel, accessible next to the "Help" button.
 Prestige Mechanic: Keep track of your Prestige, which grows through activities like purchasing trains, unlocking regions, and more. Prestige decay ensures active gameplay, adding a new layer of strategy.
🎯 Map Targets and Achievements:

 Complete map targets with achievements to "win" the map and earn stars based on the difficulty level.
🌅 Visual & UI Improvements:

 Dynamic Daylight: Enjoy beautiful daylight color changes based on the sun’s angle.
 Enhanced Minimap: Navigate with ease thanks to color-coded rails, optimized icon sizes, and new icons for village production.
⚖️ Balancing Adjustments:

 Loans & Region Prices: I’ve fine-tuned loan rates and region prices, with adjustments based on the number of regions you have unlocked.
🐞 Bug Fixes:

 I’ve squashed several bugs, including terrain holes, UI layout issues, and tooltip glitches. Plus, improvements to signal placement and locomotive replacement ensure smoother gameplay.
⚙️ Engine Update:

 I’ve upgraded to Unity 6 LTS for better performance and to prepare for future enhancements.

🗣️ Your Feedback Matters
Your feedback is invaluable to me! I’m committed to listening to your suggestions and improving Train World based on what you share. Please keep the feedback coming—I’m always looking for ways to make the game better for you.
🚆 Coming Soon: Train World Driver Beta
I’m also excited to announce that the Train World Driver Beta is just around the corner! Stay tuned for more information on how you can get involved and experience the next evolution of Train World.

Thank you for your continued support and passion for Train World. Let’s keep building something amazing together!

Happy railroading!

notes.title: Enhanced Visuals, Camera Improvements, and New Locomotives!
notes.content:
Hello Engineers,

I'm thrilled to share the latest round of updates for Train World! These changes focus on making your experience even smoother, more visually appealing, and customizable. Here's what you can expect in these latest updates:

🔍 Enhanced Camera Controls & Views 

Added a variety of new camera views for following trains, perfect for watching your locomotives from fresh angles.
Updated the camera-follow UI, along with convenient key bindings for switching views.
Improved settings to unlock camera rotation when zooming out and fixed camera height issues.
Adjusted render distance settings to control max camera height and improve performance for lower-spec systems. 
🚉 New & Updated Locomotives 

New Arrivals: Third-era diesel locomotives FM H-24-66, C 30-7, and second-era GP 7!
Model Updates: GP9, C44-9W "Dash 9," and the Mikado locomotive received improvements for a better visual experience. 
🌆 City, Station, and Depot Upgrades 

New Feature: Cities can now be renamed! Plus, station, depot, and train names will update automatically when city names change.
Terminals usage tab: Now, view how many trains use each terminal for multi-terminal stations in the station pick panel. 
📈 Refined Economy & Sorting Options 

Enhanced sorting and filtering in the "Trains" and "Economy" panels, now saving your preferences across sessions.
Graphs in the economy panel have been upgraded for better clarity, along with improved filter behavior.
New line charts in the economy panel, replacing bar charts for select stats. 
🌿 Immersive Environment Updates 

Updated grass models now feature height variations for a more natural look.
Improved oil pump models with unique animations for each era, alongside enhancements to station and depot models to refine the visual quality.
Grass, Level of Detail, and Depth of Field now respond to render distance settings, giving you more control over visuals. 
🚂 Streamlined Gameplay Features 

Quick Save: Easily save your game at any time with the new “U” key binding.
Improved tutorial sections, including new content on train creation, editing, management, waypoint optimization, and route setups.
Enhanced train list usability in various panels, plus a new reset option for custom train list filters. 
Thank you for your ongoing support and feedback; it truly drives these updates. I hope these changes make your Train World journey even more engaging and enjoyable!

Happy Railroading!

notes.title: Double Specializations, New Locomotives, and More!
notes.content:
Dear Engineers,

I’m excited to share a series of updates to Train World that bring fresh features, improvements, and significant gameplay enhancements. These updates will have a major impact on your rail empire, particularly with the new economic dynamics. 

Major Economy Update: Double Specialization Per Region
One of the most impactful changes is the new double specialization feature for regions, revolutionizing how you manage your economy:
 
 Each region now supports two specializations, providing greater production diversity and more complex logistics challenges. 
 Cities can now host two production facilities, doubling their output potential and offering new strategies for resource management. 
 Maps have been updated to reflect these changes, and I’ve improved the UI to make it easier to manage the expanded economy system. 

This update drastically enhances gameplay by giving you more control over your production chains, unlocking deeper strategic planning as you expand your rail empire.

New Locomotives & Train Management Improvements
First, let’s talk about the new locomotives:
 
 First-Era Steam Locomotives: The 0-4-4 T Onward and 2-6-6 T Mason are now available, adding new historical depth to your early rail networks. 
 Third-Era Diesel Locomotives: Modernize your railways with the powerful F 40 PH and SD 70ACe T4. 
 Locomotive parameters for the Mogul and PS 10 have been updated to improve their overall performance and efficiency. 

Improved Train Management Tools
Several new features have been added to help you keep your trains running smoothly:
 
 A new “Lifespan is at the end” warning icon helps you keep your fleet in top shape. 
 Utilization and Wait Time sorting options have been added to the Economy panel to help you locate inefficiencies quickly.
 Train Filters & Layout: Train lists in the Trains and Economy panels now have expanded filtering options, allowing for faster and more detailed management. Plus, a new Minimize/Maximize button has been added to streamline your interface. 

New Tutorials & UI Enhancements
Several new tutorial sections have been added to help players navigate complex game mechanics:
 
 Rail Types and Color-Coding: Learn more about how rail types affect your routes and how to interpret color-coding during construction. 
 Fast Rail Construction and Advanced Signal Operations: New sections provide detailed insights into optimizing your rail network. 
 Waypoint Options and Route Optimizations: Improve the efficiency of your train routes with a deeper dive into waypoints and route planning. 

The Signals panel UI has also been updated, and I’ve added improvements to the Construction UI for a smoother experience when planning and expanding your network.

Other Updates and Fixes
Here are some additional improvements and bug fixes across various aspects of the game:
 
 The lumber cargo model for all platform wagons has been updated. 
 Fixed bugs related to signal tooltips, train jumping, and rail construction near junctions. 
 Increased wagon limit: You can now have up to 250 wagons per train. 
 Numerous UI updates to the Economy and Information panels, including fixing data presentation and improving layout clarity. 

I’m committed to continuing to improve Train World based on your feedback and ideas. This update is a significant step forward, and I hope these new features enhance your gameplay experience. Don’t forget to share your thoughts and experiences in the community forums!

Stay tuned for more exciting updates, and thank you for your continued support!

notes.title: New Features, Fixes, and One-Week Demo Access!
notes.content:
Hello, Train World Engineers!

I am excited to bring you the latest update, Version 1.17.50, packed with new content, improvements, and bug fixes. Alongside this update, we are thrilled to announce that the Demo version of Train World will be available for one week! During this time, you can explore one map and research the entire first era. Don’t miss this chance to experience the game if you haven’t already!

Here’s a detailed look at what’s new:

New Locomotives and Research Updates

First-Era Steam Locomotives Added:

0-4-4 T Onward
2-6-6 T Mason
New Second-Era Diesel Locomotive: DT-6-6-2000
Research tree updates, including increased availability for RS1 and VO 1000.
Adjustments to the Mogul and PS 10 locomotive parameters for better balance.

Expanded and Improved Tutorials

New Tutorial Sections:

Research Tutorial
Regions and Production
Rails Directions Markings and Basic Signals Operations
Reputation Management
Stations and Depots
One-Time Contracts
Tutorial Map Update: The map has been updated in preparation for a future expansion of the tutorial scope.
Fixed various minor tutorial bugs, including missing buttons and UI elements.

Enhanced Signal System

New Signal Line Options: You can now customize signal behavior with three choices:

Main: Trains pass as usual (default).
Branch: Trains avoid the signal if possible.
Stop: Trains only pass if the signal is set as a waypoint.
Line Type Filters: Added options to filter/block passenger or freight trains at signals.
Added a Conditional Stop Waypoint feature, improving route efficiency by allowing trains to skip unnecessary waypoints.
Various fixes to the signal system, including correct distance labeling and improved UI interactions.
Gameplay Improvements and Bug Fixes

Gameplay Improvements and Bug Fixes

Production Unlock Changes: Production now unlocks progressively with research, rather than at era switches.
Updated the rail upgrade selector for more intuitive multi-rail upgrades.
Terrain Construction Improvements: Enhanced collision detection, terrain modification algorithms, and fixed issues like grass shaking and incorrect modifications.
Various fixes, including resolved issues with the reputation system, connection displays, and signal placements in tunnels and bridges.


Thank you for your continued support! We hope these updates enhance your Train World experience. Be sure to check out the Demo version if you’re new to the game or just want to explore the early era of rail transportation.

Happy building, and see you on the rails!

notes.title: Happy Birthday to Train World!
notes.content:
🚂🎉 Happy 1st Birthday to Train World! 🎉🚂

Today marks a special milestone as we celebrate one year since the launch of Train World! It's been an incredible journey, and I couldn't have done it without the amazing community of players and supporters.

Over the past year, I've seen Train World grow and evolve in ways I never imagined. Here are some of the exciting changes and improvements made:

 New Trains and Maps: A variety of new trains and maps have been added, enhancing your gameplay experience and expanding the world of Train World.
Overhauled Economy: The in-game economy has been completely reworked and polished, providing a more balanced and engaging experience.
New Mechanics: I introduced new mechanics such as the Reputation system and the ability to select cities for industries, adding more depth and strategy to the game.
Comprehensive Updates: Every aspect of the game has been updated or changed, ensuring a smoother and more enjoyable experience for all players.

It wasn't an easy year, but a lot was accomplished, and I am incredibly excited for what is yet to come. Your support and feedback have been invaluable, and I'm very grateful to the community. Without you, none of this would have been possible.

Here's to many more years of building, exploring, and enjoying Train World together!

All aboard for the next chapter! 🚂✨

notes.title: Biomes update, new content
notes.content:
The biomes and vegetation update cycle begins. I've updated the data structure and increased the number of biomes represented in the game. At this time changes will be minor. This first step will allow me to introduce new trees and vegetation to the biomes without map updates. Older maps will be updated with time and their appearance may change significantly. All of this will not influence previous save files. These changes will be purely visual. 

New trains were added in today's update:

 J Class is a powerful steam locomotive that bridges the gap between Big Boy and less powerful steam locomotives in the second era
 NRE 3GS is a diesel locomotive with moderate power that will be very useful in the late game for routes that do not have a lot of cargo capacity 
 ACS 64 is a powerful electric locomotive that has been requested for some time now and will be equally useful for passenger and freight operations
  Avelia Liberty will be the pinnacle of the US train tree. With a maximum speed of 350 km/h, this train brings the US into the era of high-speed trains 

Today's update also has one new map. Aurelia Atoll has an exciting donut-like shape with 2 ports. I hope this will be a welcome addition, especially for people who like to play on the smaller maps. 

In recent weeks, I focused on quality-of-life features, improvements to existing functionality, bug fixes, and adding requested features. 

Here is a list of some of the changes:

 Reputation reworked
 Updated signals placement logic
 Replace panel wagon/locomotive selection logic updated
 Improved parallel rail construction
 Improved Load panel opening speed
 Improved Load panel opening speed
 New Game UI reworked
 Alco PA/PB locomotives were replaced with EMD F7 A/B
 Added ability to assign color groups to trains
 Added floating text on maintenance and delivery payments
 Follow camera movement logic updated
 A lot of bug fixes

As for the future, I’ll continue working on biome updates, address train placement quirks (trains jump sometimes), and implement new features and content

Thank you for your interest in the project and your support.

notes.title: Industry, ports, and more
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I am happy to announce a new big update in Train World is live. Here are the changes that were made to the game since the last announcement.

New features

 Added ability to set production in the cities. Now players will have to choose where each factory goes or what cargo the city is going to produce. There are multiple strategies possible as to how you assign production: shorter distances, higher train utilization, or maximum cargo consumption. Also, players will be able to see in advance what production will be available in the future and plan rail network expansion accordingly. Cities that have production in them will show industry buildings. 
 Access to ports is now available. A nearby city will turn into a port city and will start to generate contracts to and from it. Also, ports will provide access to resources needed for production that are not available on the map. Some old maps were updated with ports as well. Port models and ship models were added.

New content

 New locomotives were added as well: a unique-looking PS-10 based on a narrow-gauge Yosemite Mountain Sugar Pine Railroad train, EL 3A was one of the first Westinghouse electric locomotives, and the famous shark nose Baldwin RF16 comes in both A and AB variants. Also, SD 40 received a model update.
 Talquell Peak is a small map with a river in the middle. Regions are small but mountains and terraces require a bit of planning from the player. At the same time, they create some very scenic views. 
 Montara Cove is a medium size map that also packs a lot of beautiful locations. The port will be a central point in gameplay here as it can access every region. You will find all kinds of terrain here from almost flat planes to mountains and valleys. 

Quality-of-life features and improvements

 All pick panels and major UI options are saved to the save file. Now you will be able to continue playing with all the pick panels open and right from the spot that you left. 
 All major panels received a key shortcut. You can change those to your liking in the settings menu.
 New localizations were added in the past weeks as well. Brazilian Portuguese, Korean, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese became available in the game.


Plans for the future

 More locomotives and trains. Many trains were never represented in the games. We know very little about a lot of interesting, cool-looking, and unique trains, and I would like to change that. 
 More maps. I believe with each map my skills in map-making are getting better and better. 
 More features to interact with cities. Adding new buildings will have an impact on cargo consumption, passenger generation, etc.
 Balancing economy, reputation update, and continuous improvements. Some tasks are just always there. 


A lot of bug fixes, improvements, and smaller changes were done during the past month. You can find a detailed description of all the changes in the Release Notes thread of the  Discussions section. More information can be found on Discord. As always, I am happy to answer all your questions in Discussions, Discord, or via e-mail. Thank you for your support and interest in the project!

notes.title: Work continues
notes.content:
The main focus of recent updates was on improving the economic aspect of both passenger and freight transportation. A lot of work was done on streamlining train creation and editing processes. The  Research section got a big update, a softer transition between eras was introduced. Several important tools were added as well, two new maps were introduced, and some visual improvements were made. Here is an overview of the changes since the last announcement. 

New stuff:

 One-time contracts are now displayed on the map
 Added ability to change one-way rail direction during station or depot during construction/edit
 Added zero start for economy data logs 
 Added data selection slider instead of only showing the last quarter
 Added data time scale for company-related graphs
 Transfer passengers have boarding priority
 Passenger loading is made proportional to waiting amounts
 Added "Mouse movement" option to enable/disable camera movement by mouse
 Unlockable locomotives and wagons have an availability duration
 Research points amount is limited to current era max usable points
 Updated train Power-to-weight labels
 Added an error icon when the wagon count is too low
 Added bridge limitations icons
 Added auto wait time option for passenger and freight trains
 Added error when construction is out of map bounds
 Added ability to remove multiple signals at once
 Added colors to boxcars, cisterns, and closed hoppers based on the carrying cargo
 Added icon for regional passengers

Maps:

 Riverrun is a small (33 X 33 km) map that represents a valley with a river in the middle with mostly agricultural industries.
 Pluma Island is a medium size (131 X 131 km) map. The island is elongated and uses only a fraction of available space which introduces challenges in expansion. Industries are leaning toward machinery and heavy industries. 

Fixes:

 The "Show route" button is inactive when cannot be used
 The train will not load if the next station on the route is the same as the current one
 The signal 3D model size increased and the position adjusted
 Fixed train balance log saving
 Fixed passenger station collision model
 Fixed Leather production facility not appearing
 Fixed research point display

 Fixed next-stop display on save load
 Fixed block-lock calculation algorithm (sometimes it triggered in wrong cases)
 Fixed unpause during train error (was locked)
 Fixed incorrect industry growth
 Fixed one-time contracts breaking
 Fixed depot price calculation
 Fixed incorrect train "Route profit" label value
 Fixed absent passenger transfer  between stations in some cases
 Fixed passengers not being picked up at the station
 Fixed regional passengers not wanting to board if the next station is not the destination while the destination is present in the route
 Fixed one-time contracts not activating
 Fixed cash level going off the bar in the taxes panel
 Fixed economy graph columns not aligning
 Fixed incorrect error order when a train is severely underpowered
 Fixed load upload station options behavior
 Updated tractor cargo model
 Fixed load/unload options not working in some circumstances
 Fixed station load/unload when the route has multiple stations connected to one city
 Fixed reputation exploit when multiple regions could be opened when time is paused
 Fixed train blocking another train from behind on some occasions
 Fixed incorrect signal position
 Fixed Alco PA model
 Fixed boxcar wagon model
 Fixed error on rail deletion in some cases
 Fixed the waypoint setting button not being accessible in some cases
 Fixed trains waiting indefinitely in auto-wait mode
 Fixed freezing on route update in some instances


Currently, I am working on the locomotives expansion list and I started to plan the next big update. 

At this point, it looks like it will be more about new features and capabilities related to cities. Also, I would like to develop a majority of tools that are needed for the introduction of realistic maps. Another aspect is visual fidelity, especially biome variety. I want to add more assets that would improve visual quality. This does not mean style changes but rather a more diverse look with less amount of repeating assets. These plans are subject to change. I will keep you informed.

Big thanks to all of you. I am very grateful for your feedback and support.

notes.title: Happy new year!
notes.content:
I wish you a Happy New Year! To be honest, this was not an easy year to put it lightly. Most important we made it. The release and first big update are behind us. A lot was achieved, mistakes were made, and a lot of knowledge and experience was picked up.

During the past week a lot of small updates and fixes were made. Here is an overview on what was done:

 Fixed train teleportation on rail/signal construction
 Fixed train teleportation on train wagons edit
 Improved incorrect direction of movement on route edit
 Reduced prices on the passenger wagons for medium era
 Numerous localization fixes
 Added station name to station options panel
 Fixed a couple of small bugs
 Fixed stuck passengers after route edit
 Fixed terminal selection
 Fixed incorrect waypoint selection after route edit
 Reputation points for region opening is lowered a bit
 Fixed estimated train speed calculations for freight trains
 Fixed incorrect lifespan calculation in certain cases
 Updated braking, trains stop a bit faster now
 Fixed passenger trains skipping wait time on signals
 Fixed train edit issues (incorrect wagon amount calculation)
 Fixed set trains edit
 Added low power cap (trains with a low power-to-weight ratio will throw an error and will not move). The fix eliminates excessive route time calculations for underpowered trains which could cause the game to hang
 Route time calculator optimized to avoid long calculation times for slow trains
 Fixed depot Electrified and High-speed rail options not updating construction correctly
 Fixed Tunnel and Garage depot rail occupation (now trains can enter and leave the Tunnel depot at the same time and not cause a block)
 Updated route selection for active trains. The train will try to get to the closest station if the new route has no rail segments that the train is on. If the train is not able to stay or get to the closest station, it will go into standby
 Fixed train and connection reputation calculations
 Adjusted reputation points needed to unlock new regions and get loans
 Added checks for transportation reward calculations so that there are no crazy numbers (division by zero, etc.)
 Rails in the map view are made darker for better visibility
 Fixed incorrect starting point selection for trains in some occasions
 Cistern wagons got a visual update (color will change depending on the transportable cargo)
 Hopper wagons also got a visual update (color will change depending on the transportable cargo)
 One-time contract fixed
 Updated hopper icons
 Fixed lifespan error disappearing too quickly
 Added option for game pause on train error (lifespan or block). The option can be disabled in the settings
 Updated map camera position clamping. The map border can be placed closer to the center of the screen

I will continue to fix bugs and improve user experience. This process is continuous and never stops. Soon, I will start the process of collecting requests for the next big update. I already got a lot of valuable feedback from you. Thank you.

I am very grateful to have such an amazing community. You helped me a lot, you motivated me and supported me. Thank you and see you next year!

notes.title: Big update arrived
notes.content:
I am happy to say that the Big update is here. In my previous announcements, I already shared some information on the changes. Here is the last part.

Reputation:

 Calculated each time the train delivers cargo. Train utilization and connection utilization are taken into account
 Reputation controls how many research points a player gets
 Low reputation will block loans or the unlocking of new regions

Achievements:

 In-game achievements are almost the same as Steam achievements, but they are unique for each session and provide an additional income stream
  Achievements are useful, especially during the early stages when cash is low

Trains inventory:

 Added inventory allows a player to keep locomotives and wagons for future use
 This is very handy for completing one-time contracts as a player does not need to sell the train or wagons after use
 Locomotives in inventory do not lose lifespan or pay maintenance

Industries:

 More than 32 industries
 Production becomes available over time and may be different based on what resources are available at the moment
 Some industries have production only in the late era (cars, tractors, etc.)
 Production may require up to 5 different components
 More than 160 cargo types are available now

Depots:

 Can be placed anywhere
 Can be selected as a waypoint. In this case, the route becomes linear and will terminate at the depot. Very useful for one-time contracts
 When launching a train, the train will always go to the first waypoint in the route

Visuals:

 Added new vegetation and animal models
 Added 2 new wagons
 Added models for new cargo types

What's next? 

 Fixing any issues that may be discovered. 
 Continue to work on train navigation and movement, quite a bit still needs to be done there. 
 Additional research on the economy model is required and more updates will be in that department. A lot was changed in the current update and things got better, but there is still room to improve. 
 The help section needs more work
 Visuals and graphics updates needed


On a larger scale: more content, locomotives, wagons, maps, and more diversity in biomes. I will start a new round of feedback collection to make a new plan for the next big update. 

Thank you for your support and interest in the project.

notes.title: Development update
notes.content:
Hi, I want to give an update on the development process for the upcoming big changes to the game. I want to give a high-level 
 overview of what is in the works and also what is planned to be added in the update. Note, that all of the things below are current state descriptions and are subject to change

Transport logic:

Passengers and freight are constantly transported by other means. The train transport now competes with these other means. So, no more situations when the production is not operating because one of the components is not delivered


Economy:

Passengers are separated into two categories: local and regional. Local passengers want to travel to the neighboring cities. Regional passengers want to travel between neighboring capitals 
The player is able to set a price level per connection. This influences the number of passengers generated by the connection. The relationship is not linear so it allows for various strategies in passenger transport
Freight transport is also split into two categories: one-time contracts and recurring deliveries. One-time contracts pay a fixed sum of money for a specific cargo delivered to the neighboring capital. Recurring requires a constant flow of cargo from the source to the destination. Recurring deliveries are split into batches. A player is able to adjust batch sizes that will be transported
Transportation profits were significantly reworked. Now profits are calculated from actual spending (maintenance and train cost) and a set margin 


Maps and industries:

Maps will be significantly updated, and regions will be changed. Expect city density closer to the one seen in the "Noran Island" map.  The number of cities per region is reduced to four including the capital. So "Noran Isand" will have five regions
Each region will have industry specialization with production centered around that specialization
Regions do not have default consumption. This was replaced by industry-centered deliveries and one-time contracts
Production facilities appear on the map as the player progresses with the game and the type of facilities that appear is random and depends on available resources
The plan is to have over twenty industry specializations with more than a hundred production facilities and cargo types


Trains:

Trains are split into passenger and freight. Passenger trains will never be able to become freight trains and vice versa
Lines were removed, and now trains have routes that a set per train. While cloning a train a player has an option to include the route
Depots were added. Now the train has to get to the route from the closest depo
Routes can end at the depot. This way the route will not be looped (very useful for one-time contracts)
Cargo types are grouped (liquid, bulk, etc.). Now wagons and stations transport specific groups
Added locomotives lifespan. When the train reaches the end of its lifespan the power drops significantly to the point that the train stops.  Lifespan affects sell price
Added adjustable maintenance. Higher maintenance will cost more, but expend lifespan of the locomotive
A few wagons will be added


UI:

Will reflect all the changes as well as some minor updates and improvements


I will provide information on other changes in the next announcements. I hope you will like the changes. 

Important, previous saves will not be compatible with the new version. I will try to keep the old version of the game available on a separate branch.

notes.title: Work progress
notes.content:
As promised the game continues to be updated, new features are added and issues are addressed. I constantly publish updates with fixes and new features. I try to swiftly react to the issues or requests that the players have. Below is a list of features that were added/updated/fixed during the past 3 weeks.
Features added:

Added a toggle to the map view that will keep the map camera position on the view changes
Added per-platform maintenance for multi-platform stations
Added signals auto placement tool (allows instant placing of multiple signals)
Added ability to rebind controls. In the tutorial, default controls will be used. Help also will reference default controls. Keys like Esc, Tab (for view switch), and cursor keys could not be changed
Added sandbox game mode where a player can choose: starting era, unlock all regions, unlock all research within the starting era, infinite money, and keep all unlocked locomotives and wagons from all eras in the store. Achievements are disabled for sandbox mode
Added double rail construction. Junctions and crossings should be done via single-rail construction. Everything else is the same as with regular rail construction
Added email subscription for Turn Point Games. This will be used only for major announcements

Updated features:

Taxes made more aggressive for difficulty setting "Hard"
Updated rail construction (reduced number of overlapping errors)
Signals assigned to lines can be removed via the UI panel
Updated signals panel and help section
Improved stability during level/save loading
Updated map contour lines, added a second set of contour lines, and improved graphics
Increased zoom-in value on the map (zoom closer to the surface is possible now)
Parallel bridges and tunnels will update together if they share structures
When two trains lock each other the error message will turn red. This will help identify locked trains faster
Updated minimap, an alternative way to display relevant information was introduced. This should eliminate crashes due to memory leaks
Guides in the world view, were made semi-transparent to improve the rail construction experience
 The second press on the pause will set the previous time scale
Reduced research points generation. After the introduction of the X16 time scale, a player could go through the first era too quickly 
Updated rails appearance and speed limits. The first-era speed limit is set to 100 km/h (60 mi/h). Upon entering the second era all rails automatically upgrade to the maximum speed of 160 km/h (100 mi/h). In the third era, regular rail's maximum speed stays at 160 km/h (100 mi/h) with the unlockable ability to build/upgrade to the high-speed rails at 320 km/h (200 mi/h).

Issues fixed:

Fixed loan button being disabled on some occasions
Fixed price display for trains bulk replace
Fixed guides showing in the mini-map after deletion
Fixed error in the help menu
Fixed 3rd era missing locomotives
Fixed missing passenger connections (old saves and new games)
Fixed station replacement not activating the connection
Fixed a number of achievements
Fixed ability to place station that collides with other stations
Fixed "End game" on negative company value
Fixed train maintenance reducing general maintenance
Fixed rails slope/height resetting when confirming rail construction via UI
Fixed Steam cloud saves not deleting
Fixed error during signal placement
Fixed train errors not updating on train edit
Fixed passenger trains "jumping" at the station on some occasions
Fixed error on train assignment to lines that have no path
Fixed parallel bridges and tunnels not presenting correctly
Fixed an ability to switch time scale during construction via keyboard
Fixed Alco PAPB price, some other trains got their prices and 

I am very grateful for your support. More is coming.

notes.title: Quality updates
notes.content:
The new game update is live. Here is the list of changes:
- A lot of backend fixes
- A player now has the ability to remove stations and signals that are assigned to lines
- It is possible to delete or modify rails occupied by trains
- Added station "Maintenance" label to stations construction panel
- Added "Clean distance" label to rails construction panel. It displays the length of a rail section not obstructed by intersections, junctions, or signals. It is very useful for siding construction.
- Updated text field for naming and save file name edit. Added blinking cursor
- Small UI fixes in Research and Regions panels. Updated cargo icons layout for  Full HD resolution
- Lists panels are made resizable in height (trains list, lines list, etc.)
- Regions prices increase the more regions you have. For the biggest map, the maximum possible region price is 31 million

I will continue working on improving the quality of the game as well as polishing various aspects. Also, I am constantly going through the list of requests and checking which ones I can implement right away and the rest are integrated into the future development. 

The decision was made to disable the demo and focus on the game improvements and feature development. The demo will be disabled on August 20, 2023. It served its purpose and now the demo takes too much resources to update frequently. Also, having two versions of the game increases the chance of making a mistake.

Thank you for your interest in the project and see you around.

notes.title: New maps
notes.content:
Two new maps are added in the last update:

 Small Nordic island that has only 4 regions
 Large map with a massive lake in the middle

Feedback on the maps is very important, I will be happy to hear what you think about new and existing maps. 

A couple of suggestions are also included in the update. Station and rail construction maintains your last selected options, no need to pick high-speed rails every time. The same is done for train and line sorting.

Also, a lot of work is being done on improving quality. I am highly determined to bring quality to the highest possible level. I am trying to address all your concerns and questions in a timely manner and will continue to do it in the future.

Thank you for your support and will see you around!

notes.title: Train World is live
notes.content:
The game is released. What does it mean for Train World? This means you have a chance to support me in future project development of new content and features. You now have a real impact on what happens next. Your feedback and support are crucial for the project. 

A few updates have already been published, most are about bug fixes. There are also a few changes:

 added v-sync option, this could help with screen tearing and the smoothness of the game
 difficulty setting is now available. It influences money income, loans, and taxes. Current saves will not be influenced by this
 I've added X 16 time scale button. This should make the game more comfortable and reduce moments where you need to wait for long periods of time. Note, with this change I had to remove the ability for the camera to follow the train at X8 and X16 time speed. This is done to remove any chance of issues when following high-speed trains


Long term, the plan is to add more maps, more game modes, and of course trains. I am planning to release a series of maps of various sizes so we together could find a sweet spot for the size and density of the maps. No money/everything open game mode is in the plans as well. Longer term, European trains set.

Again, thank you for your feedback and support, see you around.

notes.title: Major Demo Update
notes.content:
Hi, finally, I can present you our big demo update.  

I am also happy to say that we are moving closer to the point where we will be able to release the game. I hope to make a release date announcement very soon. 

Here is a list of what was introduced and changed in a recent update:

 Updated signals mechanic. Now signals can be used as waypoints.
 Added "No stop" mechanic. Signal blocks train from stopping on a certain section of tracks. 
 Signals icons on the map represent the current signal state and switch accordingly
 Added station parameters: loading, unloading, wait time, etc.
 Added expandable freight station that can serve all types of wagons. 
 Updated passenger generation.
 Updated economy, added useful data about trains to the economy window (wait time, utilization)
 Updated UI (icons, cursors, UI fixes)
 Added "Bulk replace" mechanic, that allows replacement of a certain wagon or a locomotive
 Maps updated. A dedicated tutorial map was added.
 Improved rail construction. 
 Added an ability to view track usage, track direction, and signal states in a special construction overlay.
 Train block error now contains the name of the train that is blocking the path.
 Updated graphics and color scheme.
 A lot of bug fixes and quality improvements. 

Also, a lot of work was made on the systems that are not present in the Demo. 

Unfortunately, old save files will not work with the new update.

notes.title: Signals update and future development
notes.content:
Hi, here is a list of what was added and changed in a recent update:

 Added icons for signals to the map
 Added icons for the disconnected rail segments
 Updated signal placement and edit
 Updated signal panel
on the remove button on the signal panel
 Added button for switching construction view
 Added rail direction/usage lines

To edit the signal: click on it to select and then click again to change the direction or click on the button on the signals panel.

To remove the signal: click on the signal icon to select it and then "Left Click + Right Ctrl" or click 

Lines on top of the rails display which direction the trains can go. Green line - the rail track is not occupied and the red line - the rail track is occupied

Known issue: in some occasions, signals may not load correctly from the save file. This will be fixed after the next big update. 

It will take a while for the next update. I am planning to have a lot of major changes. The majority of those changes will be under the hood and will not affect gameplay. Unfortunately, the next big update will not be compatible with the current saved files. I hope this will be the only time I have to break persistence between saved files.

notes.title: Regular update.
notes.content:
Hi, Train World Fans!

I am happy to present an interactive tutorial step-by-step for Train World. I got a lot of feedback that it is a challenge for newcomers to start playing and I wanted to make sure that there is a tool for new players to learn how to play the game.

Based on your feedback, I've updated the camera controls and expanded camera rotation angles. The train 'Follow camera' got a major update and now can be positioned with more freedom. 

You can now switch off the UI by pressing the 'K' key on the keyboard. This will be useful for making screenshots and videos. 

Thank you for your support and feedback!
